messages:
Raj Patel: FYI — after the peering change in us-west2 (~02:15) we started seeing persistent tail IOPS on local NVMe. GPU pods failing to provision because nodes are stuck in IO wait. graphs: https://grafana.company/uid/abc123?panel=nvme_tail
Marie Chen: Seen it. nvme_write_latency p95 jumped ~6x at the same timestamp. Background GC/janitor threads ramped on a subset of nodes. Logs show 'flush queue full' and repeated retried writes.
Lucas Nguyen: Is this the peering ACL change that rerouted control-plane metadata over a slower path? If metadata syncs are delayed then ephemeral writebacks can pile up.
Ava Torres: Can we throttle janitor/scrub on affected pools temporarily? Lower concurrency or pause scrubs until stable. e.g. set janitor.concurrency=2 for the pool.
Raj Patel: Applying canary config to 3 nodes now: gnode-uw2-143/117/102. Command I ran:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"2"}}'
```
Infra Oncall Bot: Detected configmap patch in infra namespace by raj.patel — rolling restart scheduled for janitor-daemonset (3 pods) :gear:
Marie Chen: After the canary change, one of the nodes showed kernel blk messages and one GPU driver timeout. snippet from /var/log/kern.log:
```
[02:18:34] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[02:18:36] nvme nvme0: controller lost
```
Lucas Nguyen: Immediate mitigation: cordon the 3 noisy nodes to stop new GPU scheduling and reduce pressure. Also push a quick iptables rule rollback if peering change is the root cause.
SIE-ops: Cordoned gnode-uw2-143, gnode-uw2-117, gnode-uw2-102 — no new GPU pods will schedule. :white_check_mark:
Raj Patel: Provisioning success rate climbing back toward baseline after cordon + janitor throttle on canary. We'll keep the canary for 30m and decide whether to rollback peering ACL change if it doesn't stabilize.
Ava Torres: Opening an incident ticket IR-2026-331, tagging SRE + Networking. Adding the grafana links, kernel snippets, and node list. I'll also push a temporary autoscaler tweak to avoid aggressive launches in us-west2.
Marie Chen: Post-mortem action items I think: (1) add janitor backoff when NVMe latency crosses threshold, (2) improve control-plane peering safeguards for metadata syncs, (3) add an automatic cordon playbook for GPU provisioning impact. Short notes saved in the incident.
Raj Patel: Thanks — will follow up with timeline + rollback plan. If anyone sees new errors from other regions call it out here. :raised_hands:
